feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital communications/platform leadership, with clear progression, relevant scope, and solid public-sector positioning. It reads polished and substantive, but it is somewhat dense and repetitive, and could sharpen impact by reducing overlap and adding more outcome-focused evidence.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong career progression within NACo, culminating in director-level ownership of web, analytics, governance, and multimedia.  
- Good credibility signals: specific platforms, tools, scale metrics, and concrete projects make the profile believable and relevant.  
- Writing is generally polished and professional, with consistent tone and strong domain alignment for digital/public-sector roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” “Technical + IT,” and “Recent Projects” overlap heavily; consolidate to improve scannability and structure.  
- Increase measurable impact: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results; add outcomes such as engagement gains, efficiency improvements, adoption, or campaign performance.  
- Tighten style consistency: use parallel bullet structure and standardize punctuation around lists. Minor style issues include inconsistent serial commas (“web, email, social, and multimedia” vs. elsewhere), “organization-wide”/“organization’s” repetition, and slightly awkward phrasing like “French (A2/Learning).” No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and work experience. Tightening it and foregrounding the most relevant strengths will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consider: “Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing enterprise web ecosystems for high-volume public-sector organizations. Builds and leads governance, analytics, editorial, and multimedia systems that improve publishing operations, audience insight, and user experience, including AI-enabled content discovery.”
- Replace “building the platforms” with more active, outcome-oriented phrasing like “modernizing enterprise web ecosystems” or “leading digital platform transformation.”
- Simplify the long list of functions; group related areas to improve scanability.
- Use “organizations” once; avoid repeating “complex, mission-driven organizations” if the rest of the CV already proves that context.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with Core Competencies and Recent Projects; “AI-enabled content discovery” is more specific.
- “Governance models,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “editorial systems” are repeated elsewhere, so keep the intro higher-level.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and work experience. It would be stronger if tightened to emphasize distinctive capability areas rather than repeating broad phrases already used elsewhere.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use shorter, sharper labels and align wording with the most senior/recent scope: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance • Editorial operations • Analytics infrastructure • AI search experiences • Workflow automation • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production
- Replace “Digital governance & editorial systems” with “Digital governance and editorial operations” for clearer business impact and less jargon.
- Consider changing “Multi-channel communications operations” to “Cross-channel communications leadership” to sound more senior and less process-heavy.
- Standardize style: either use all “and” or all “&”; avoid mixing operational phrases with platform phrases.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “AI-enabled…experiences” repeat the header almost verbatim.
- This section also overlaps substantially with Topline Skills; keep competencies broader and let later sections carry the tool/detail specificity.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it largely repeats achievements already covered in Work Experience. Tightening the phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it feel more distinctive and higher impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected recent projects” framing to reinforce recency and context.
- Use parallel, tighter phrasing: “Led/Built/Developed…” and trim filler like “designed for continued campaign growth.”
- Add 1 concrete result, audience, or scale detail where possible (e.g., users, campaign reach, conference/event context, stakeholder group).
- Standardize style and punctuation; spell out “10-by-20-foot” for consistency in formal CV writing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, and advocacy video series closely overlap with current NACo consultant and prior NACo bullets; keep this section more project-specific than role-summary.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most distinct item; consider emphasizing it first if you want this block to add new information.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with earlier NACo entries and the Recent Projects section. Tighten it around consultant-level outcomes, platform modernization, and the AI/search work.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancement, content operations, and enterprise web modernization for member-facing communications.”
- Consolidate overlapping bullets into 3–4 impact-focused lines, e.g.:
- “Designed and implemented Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, and downloadable member toolkits.”
- “Improved cross-channel communications operations by refining web workflows, analytics, governance, and publishing standards.”
- “Led an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content requirements, and discovery UX for complex policy content.”
- Replace generic phrases like “deliver technical troubleshooting” with stronger verbs: “implemented,” “optimized,” “streamlined,” “modernized.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: number of sites/pages supported, workflow time reduced, engagement gains, search success improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, usability, and operational best practices” repeats themes from Director of Digital Media.
- Microsite and AI-search details also appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics. It should be tightened to emphasize enterprise ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with the earlier NACo role’s newsletter/video execution details.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope statement: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Combine the website bullets into one impact-led line: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership outcome-focused: replace “reaching tens of thousands” / “serving thousands” with stronger metrics if available (subscriber growth, engagement rate, open rate, follower growth, campaign performance).
- Tighten operations bullets: “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to improve decision-making and governance.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Managed newsletters” and “expanded video programming” overlap with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on leadership, modernization, and systems.
- Governance/editorial workflow language also appears elsewhere; frame it here as enterprise-wide operational leadership.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads broad and overlaps with the more senior NACo roles. Make it sharper by emphasizing what you owned at this level and any concrete scale or outcomes.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + ownership: “Managed day-to-day digital communications operations across NACo’s web, email, social and video channels, supporting advocacy messaging and cross-team editorial execution.”
- Tighten bullets to distinct contributions: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Rephrase video bullet to show growth/creation: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets and add outcome if available: “Built stronger editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving coordination and content consistency.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video” overlaps with the Director of Digital Media entry; keep this version focused on execution rather than leadership/governance.
- Weekly advocacy video also appears in the earlier 2015–2018 role and footer project list; avoid repeating “weekly video updates” without a differentiating result.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this skills block is too generic and overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo roles. Tighten it to emphasize senior-level scope and distinct value rather than broad communications language.

Suggested edit
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, leadership-level wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & web modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing workflows & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership (web, email, social, video)
- Public-sector advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content strategy
- Keep parallel structure; avoid mixing nouns (“strategy”) with softer descriptors (“focused”).
- If space allows, make one item more outcome-oriented, e.g. “Enterprise digital strategy for high-volume public-sector communications.”
- Consider dropping “messaging” and “content planning,” which read less senior than the rest of the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy,” “editorial systems and governance,” and “multi-channel communications” repeat Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” is already well established in the header and work experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill coverage, but this item is too tool-heavy and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, it should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and modernization themes, with only the most relevant tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a software list to a capability-led line: “Drupal and enterprise CMS platforms • Website modernization and migration • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API and workflow integrations • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or older-feeling items like jQuery unless it is still central to recent work.
- Prioritize recent, proven strengths from NACo work: Drupal, CMS modernization, integrations/workflows, and AI-enabled search.
- If space allows, sharpen impact language: “Enterprise CMS modernization” or “Platform integration and automation” reads stronger than generic “technical execution.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, HTML/CSS/JavaScript, API integrations, and Airtable already appear in “Technical + IT.”
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also repeats the header/core competencies; keep it here only if you trim elsewhere.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a tool list and overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT.” In Topline Skills, this should emphasize strategic analytics leadership and business impact more than platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools-first to outcomes-first, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI frameworks and executive reporting” before listing platforms.
- Tighten to 5–7 items and group related tools: “GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio and Power BI” rather than separate bullets for each.
- Replace “Leadership reporting” with stronger phrasing like “Executive dashboards and decision support.”
- Consider rewrite: “Analytics strategy • KPI framework design • Executive dashboards and decision support • GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio and Power BI • User behavior analysis (Microsoft Clarity) • SEO and performance optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item substantially duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep Topline Skills strategic and leave full tool inventory to Technical + IT.
- “SEO and performance analysis” may overlap with broader analytics language; use “optimization” if you want a more senior, action-oriented tone.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the Core Competencies line and several NACo bullets. Make it more distinctive by emphasizing production infrastructure and event execution rather than generic “video production.”

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: **Broadcast & Event Production** — Video production and post-production • Livestream and webcast delivery • PTZ camera and control-room workflows • Studio buildout and operations • Hybrid and virtual event production
- Replace “editing” with **post-production** for a more senior, systems-level tone.
- Consider adding one concrete scale marker if true, e.g., **broadcast-quality studio operations** or **multi-camera livestream delivery**.
- Keep this skills block focused on capabilities not already covered elsewhere; let work experience carry the outcomes.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestream operations” already appears in Core Competencies; avoid repeating the exact phrase.
- “Studio operations” and “video” are already evidenced in the Director of Digital Media and Associate Communications Director entries, so this section should stay concise.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. Use this space to signal depth and recency, with Drupal clearly leading.

Suggested edit
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Add light qualifiers to show level of use: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites, governance) • WordPress (site administration) • SharePoint / Power Pages (internal and low-code platforms) • GitHub Pages (lightweight static sites)**
- If space allows, make Drupal more outcome-linked: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; 3.5M annual page views)** to reinforce impact from recent roles.
- Consider retitling to **CMS & Web Platforms** for cleaner phrasing.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; avoid repeating the same plain list in both places.
- If you add Drupal outcomes here, keep the topline skills version shorter and more category-based.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior recent-profile CV, tighten it to tools that signal implementation depth and modern delivery.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Front-End Development & Technical Delivery**
- Replace with a sharper list: **HTML5/CSS3 • JavaScript • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions/CI-CD**
- Drop **jQuery** unless it is still actively used in recent work; if kept, place last or label as legacy support.
- If space allows, add one proof point in adjacent experience bullets instead of here, e.g. “implemented custom Drupal front-end components, GTM tagging, and API-driven features.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This duplicates **HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery** plus **API integrations** already listed under Topline Skills.
- **Workflow automation** and **AI-enabled search experiences** are covered elsewhere; avoid expanding this item into those areas.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. Since “workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear elsewhere, this item should be tighter and more category-led.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe by function, not just brand names: “Workflow automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/issue management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Team collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams”
- Put the strongest, most relevant tools first: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana.
- Consider trimming lower-value/general tools if space is tight; Slack and Teams are widely assumed unless central to systems leadership.
- If possible, connect to scope in a nearby summary line, e.g., “Built cross-team workflow and intake systems” or “Supported editorial planning and automation across communications operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable systems” and “Workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills, so avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp overlap as project tools; listing all four may feel redundant unless each was materially used.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too bare to add much value on its own. It should signal level of use and enterprise relevance, especially since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize platform scope, not just tool names: “Email & Engagement Platforms: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp”
- If accurate, add qualifiers that show depth: “enterprise email automation,” “member communications,” or “newsletter operations” tied to the strongest/most recent platforms.
- Put the most relevant/current platform first; if Dynamics 365 is the newest enterprise-grade tool, keep it first.
- Consider trimming to the 2 strongest systems if one was only lightly used.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- This overlaps with multiple work bullets about leading email newsletters and digital channels; avoid repeating operational detail here.
- “Higher Logic” and “Mailchimp” may feel dated unless supported by recent or substantial use.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and largely duplicates the “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills and the NACo work bullets. Tighten it to emphasize methods and business use, not just another tool list.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics & Optimization Tools**
- Replace with: **GA4 • BigQuery • Power BI • Looker Studio • Microsoft Clarity • Google Tag Manager • KPI reporting • dashboard development • SEO analysis • experimentation**
- Put the strongest/recent tools first: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Clarity.
- Use parallel, more specific phrasing: swap “Dashboarding” for “dashboard development” and “A/B testing” for “experimentation” unless you’ve directly run formal tests.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills: Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider trimming one of the two or making this section tools-only.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already named in the 2022–2024 NACo role, so avoid repeating the exact same framing here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and overlaps with later NACo roles. Make it more execution-focused and specific to foundational team-building and production contributions.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to emphasize scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and formalize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add clearer ownership and outcomes: “Supported a major website refresh and produced recurring digital content, including livestreams and weekly video updates, to expand the organization’s in-house publishing capacity.”
- Tighten the management point: “Provided day-to-day direction to a digital media associate” instead of “guidance.”
- If possible, add 1–2 metrics: number of livestreams/videos produced, audience growth, publishing volume, or efficiency gains from workflow improvements.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; distinguish this entry as launching or piloting the format.
- Team-building/workflow language also appears in later roles; keep this item focused on early implementation rather than leadership.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Emphasize the innovation/program support angle and keep the media work concise.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground scope and first-of-its-kind impact: “Coordinated county innovation and research initiatives that supported NACo program development and policy communications.”
- Tighten the media portion: “Produced digital and multimedia content for member-facing communications, including launching NACo’s first podcast from concept through scripting and production.”
- If possible, add outcomes: number of projects supported, podcast episodes launched, audiences reached, or departments/program teams served.
- Consider splitting into two clauses only; avoid listing too many production tasks since later roles cover broader digital execution.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager/Producer and Associate Communications Director entries.
- Podcast/video production themes recur elsewhere; keep this item focused on origin/launch rather than ongoing multimedia leadership.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads more like a mix of software and capabilities. It also overlaps with “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” and several work bullets, so tighten it to tool-specific terms and keep only distinctive production capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to **Creative & Production Tools** for clearer scope.
- Separate software from workflows; use more standard phrasing:  
  **Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Livestream production workflows • Podcast recording/editing**
- If accurate, add stronger/specific tools instead of generic workflow language, e.g. streaming platforms, switchers, or audio tools.
